claims.text: Selective laser melting at a linear energy density of at least 2.83 J/mm can form a single BCC solid solution in NbMoTaWVCr.
SLM of NbMoTaW at a linear energy density around 2.83 J/mm produces a single BCC solid solution.
SPS of gas-atomized, low-oxygen HfNbTaTiZr powder can produce a fully dense specimen.
HPT following SPS can refine HfNbTaTiZr to a grain size below 500 nm.
The combined SLM, SPS, and HPT route will produce a nanocrystalline single-BCC NbMoTaWVCr alloy with grain size below 500 nm.
Use of gas-atomized low-oxygen powder is important for achieving dense material that can subsequently be refined by HPT.
Vacuum or inert-atmosphere processing will minimize interstitial contamination.
The high cooling rate of SLM prevents segregation of high-melting elements in NbMoTaWVCr.
SPS homogenization and HPT prevent formation of Laves, silicide, and B2 phases in the proposed alloy.
Fine grains increase strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Interstitial solid solutions and lattice friction strengthen refractory high-entropy alloys.
Controlled low-level oxygen or nitrogen stabilizes the proposed nanocrystalline single-BCC matrix.
Removing brittle Laves, silicide, and B2 secondary phases should mitigate ambient-temperature brittleness.
Conventional liquid-state processing of refractory HEAs can cause elemental segregation or evaporation.
NbMoTaWVCr containing interstitial solid solution and fine grains has previously reached a yield strength of 3416 MPa and plasticity of 5.3% at room temperature.
The proposed SLM, SPS, and HPT product will have yield strength above 1400 MPa.
The proposed product will exhibit elongation above 20%.
The proposed product will have excellent high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The proposed single-BCC nanocrystalline state will retain structural integrity at temperatures up to about 1050 degrees Celsius.
Interstitial content above its solubility limit will cause excessive oxide formation and invalidate the strategy.

contradictions.description: SPS of gas-atomized powder is presented as post-processing of an SLM-fabricated alloy, but SPS ordinarily consolidates powder and the hypothesis does not explain how an already SLM-built component becomes the gas-atomized powder feedstock. The evidence supports SLM and SPS/HPT as separate routes, not this sequential route.
The scope is labeled as Group IV-V transition-metal alloys, while the principal NbMoTaWVCr example contains Mo, W, and Cr, which are Group VI elements.

The mediator and mechanism require a single BCC phase and absence or elimination of brittle secondary phases, whereas the falsification rule permits up to 5% brittle intermetallic phase without falsifying the hypothesis.
